ratings_why.fun: Over a 7 because every recruit turn asks a real question with no single right answer: which fish step into the front row, who stands beside the redd to catch the gift, and whether to cash a hoard now through the Grandfather or keep feeding Kype and Llyn Llyw.
ratings_why.distinct: Earning a counter by surviving and choosing when to go home is fresh, but Little Jack and Bradán are a familiar Brann/Rivendare-style repeater pair, and the gift feels a little like Oozes' eating.

verdict_why: The homecoming chain has no per-turn cap, and Rust-Flank Hen and Fry-under-repeaters need clear wording; once those are fixed it is ready to settle.

points.text: Homes are checked again until none is ready, and a Fry can turn into a fresh copy that comes home again in the same chain. Three Thumbprint Parrs with the Fish-Pass Keeper (or golden Parrs) look able to loop forever, and with the Bend-Wife that means endless stats. Cap it: each slot comes home at most once a turn.
On Rust-Flank Hen, "it gains +1/+1" could mean the Hen or the stamped unit. Name which one; the tier check suggests the Hen spreads the buff, so say "that unit".

Old Bradán and Little Jack repeat Spawn effects, but a Fry's Spawn is "becomes a fresh copy", and Mother Redd's counts spawns. Say whether a repeated Fry Spawn does anything, whether Bradán triggering Redd counts as one of her spawns, and whether a Fry keeps its Stamps when it turns.

The Passport Seller is the best off-label card here. Let golden Passport Seller give the passported unit a small Spawn (for example "Spawn: repeat its When played") so cross-tribe homecomings fire Bend-Wife, Jack and Bradán too.
The Seal-Scarred Veteran is the one card that only does its own job. Making the buff "gains +3/+3 and a Stamp" for back-row fish would tie it into the hoard build.

standouts.why: Grandfather Under the Alders bridges the two builds: hoard Stamps for Kype and Llyn Llyw, then send one fat passport home for a board-wide cash-out.
Passport Seller turns any tribe's unit into a fish, so an Ooze Belly, a Pack Hunter or a When-played unit gets a homecoming the designer only half listed.
The Bailiff of the Weir is the engine and a puzzle at once: Stamps for everyone, but every third turn he eats your smallest fish, maybe Little Jack or a Fry.

weakest.why: Seal-Scarred Veteran is a plain in-fight buff with no Stamp or Spawn hook.
Reunion Secretary asks you to count equal Stamp groups for a small buff; fiddly for what it pays.
Pilgrim Guide's 2 gold does nothing until Jack or Bradán repeats it.

flags.note: Fry turning back into a copy in the same chain, plus uncapped re-checks, looks like an infinite homecoming loop with several Parrs and the Fish-Pass Keeper.
Old Kelt's copy each turn plus the Fry's copy makes triples fast, including passported units from other tribes.
Golden Little Jack beside Old Bradán with Pilgrim Guides and the Bend-Wife multiplies gold and stats every Bradán homecoming.
"it gains +1/+1" doesn't say whether the Hen or the stamped unit gains it.
What repeating a Fry's "becomes a fresh copy" Spawn does is not stated.
